thread.title: Merz steadfast as German Jews urge unconditional support of Israel - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Merz steadfast as German Jews urge unconditional support of Israel - NewsBreak

author: DPA
title: Merz steadfast as German Jews urge unconditional support of Israel - NewsBreak
text:
By DPA ,
15 minutes ago
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz says his country remains committed to the security of Israel after the Central Council of Jews in Germany called on the government to continue to support the Jewish state unconditionally.
As the council marked 75 years since its foundation on Wednesday, its president Josef Schuster called on Merz not to be "dissuaded from this path" – neither by other European countries nor by "individual lawmakers."
"Germany must stand clearly on the side of Israel," he demanded in a speech at a ceremony in Berlin.
Merz later told the ceremony that criticism of the Israeli government must be possible, and he himself has recently voiced such criticism alongside European counterparts given the Gaza war.
"But our country harms its own soul when this criticism becomes a pretext for hatred of Jews – or when it even leads to demands that the Federal Republic turn away from Israel," Merz said.
"Germany's commitment to the existence and security of the State of Israel is a non-negotiable part of the normative foundations of our country."
Germany - partly because of its Nazi past - has been one of Israel's most important backers in the wake of the Hamas-led attacks on October 7, 2023.
While the Merz administration, which took office in May, has in part been more vocal than the previous government in its criticism of Israel's campaign in the Gaza Strip, Berlin continues to oppose EU sanctions on Israel over the attacks on the Palestinian territory.
Schuster admitted that not all decisions taken by the government of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu were understandable, with Jews based outside Israel opposing statements made by some members of his Cabinet.
However, Germany must stand up for Israel's security, regardless of who is head of government, he demanded.
Increasing anti-Semitism in Germany
Founded in Frankfurt five years after the end of World War II, the Central Council of Jews in Germany considers itself the political, social and religious representative of the German Jewish community.
Schuster said the fact that the council was founded shortly after the Nazi Holocaust was a symbol of the survival and renewal of Jewish life in Germany.
Alongside increasingly anti-Israeli sentiment in Germany, the country has seen a dramatic rise in anti-Semitism, whether in classrooms, universities or on social media, according to Schuster.
Anti-Semitism is an attack on democracy, he said. "No one who incites hatred against Jews is a democrat. No one who attacks minorities has any interest in social cohesion.
"This anniversary is therefore not only a moment of joy for us, but also a mission to continue to raise our voices clearly and distinctly, also in the interests of our democracy," he added.
Merz expressed his continued shock and shame over anti-Semitism in Germany, which he said has become louder, more open, more brazen, and more violent since October 7, 2023.
Israeli restaurants, places of Jewish life, and sites of Jewish remembrance have been defaced and threatened.
"We are all called upon to show civil courage wherever we witness anti-Semitism, racism, or discrimination," Merz added.
He paid tribute to the role and contributions of the council.
"The Federal Republic would have been forever uprooted without Jewish life and Jewish culture in our country," the chancellor said.
"I want to say to the Jewish people in Germany today: Without you, there can be no good future for the Federal Republic."
